children: BTCS

Chief Executive Officer Charles Allen outlined the company’s strategy to expand its decentralized finance operations, use on-chain borrowing to manage capital and emphasize gross profit as a key performance measure during a Water Tower Research Virtual Insights Conference.

Allen said BTCS differentiates itself from other publicly traded crypto-related companies through its operating businesses, including blockchain infrastructure and its Imperium DeFi operation. The company is directionally long Ethereum, he said, but aims to generate returns through operating gross profit rather than relying solely on appreciation in ETH.

“If we can outperform ETH in terms of what it may do in terms of a return on an annual basis with gross profit, it’s a much better place to be,” Allen said. He added that Imperium is intended to act as a “shock absorber” against Ethereum price movements, allowing the company to continue operating if ETH declines or remains flat.
Expansion to Base and Other Networks

BTCS recently announced plans to expand Imperium to Base, the Ethereum Layer 2 network. Allen said the move gives the company another chain through which it can generate revenue and gross profit while remaining relatively straightforward to account for because Base is built on Ethereum.

He said the company is evaluating other chains and strategies as it seeks to make its operations more scalable. BTCS operates across NodeOps, block-building activities through Builder+, and DeFi liquidity provisioning through Imperium.

Allen described the company’s strategic shift this year toward gross profit, rather than primarily pursuing revenue growth. He said BTCS had previously expected to focus more heavily on improving margins in 2027, but management and the board decided in January to move that effort forward amid market conditions.
BTCS reported $1 million in gross profit during the first quarter, according to Allen.
The company reported $1.5 million in gross profit during the second quarter.
Management has established a $6 million gross-profit target tied to internal key performance indicators, which Allen said is not formal guidance.

Allen said the company reaffirmed its expectation of achieving that target in a press release because it had visibility into its operating progress. He said BTCS expects to provide further financial detail following the end of the third quarter.
On-Chain Capital Management

Allen said BTCS uses DeFi as a funding mechanism and described the company as the only U.S. public company doing so. He said on-chain borrowing can provide relatively low-cost capital with near-immediate availability, without the legal, underwriting and documentation processes associated with more traditional financing arrangements.

The approach allows BTCS to increase or reduce leverage as conditions change, he said. Allen contrasted that flexibility with a conventional convertible financing, which can require lengthy negotiations and may not allow capital to be repaid and redeployed as quickly.

BTCS raised $10 million that Allen said was deployed into Imperium. The company increased the loan-to-value ratio approved by its board for on-chain borrowing to 50% from about 40%, he said. Allen stated that capital deployed in Imperium rose to $36 million from $8 million at the end of the second quarter.

He said the company is not simply borrowing against Ethereum to purchase additional Ethereum. Rather, he said liquidity-provisioning positions can reduce exposure to ETH price declines and can be withdrawn quickly to repay debt if necessary. Allen noted that the structure can also limit upside because positions may shift into stablecoins when ETH rises.
Regulation, Ethereum Exposure and Reporting Challenges

Allen discussed recent U.S. regulatory developments, including the failure of the CLARITY Act in the Senate and what he described as new SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission frameworks. He said he believes regulatory developments permitting tokenized equities and providing a clearer operating environment could support more on-chain activity, which could create additional fee opportunities for BTCS.
His comments represented his view of the potential policy implications. Allen said the company is also evaluating potential opportunities involving tokenized assets.

On market risk, Allen acknowledged that BTCS remains directionally long ETH and said the company reduced its Ethereum position during an earlier market downturn. He described Imperium’s growth from $8 million to $36 million in deployed capital as an added protective element. Allen also said he believes Ethereum could benefit from institutional tokenization activity, citing his view that most tokenized real-world assets are built on Ethereum.

Allen said accounting standards remain a challenge for crypto-focused public companies. He argued that current U.S. accounting rules may not fully reflect the economic value of crypto holdings or DeFi positions, and said investors should focus on revenue, gross profit and operating scale when assessing BTCS.
“The proof’s going to be in the pudding,” Allen said, adding that management believes financial performance will be central to demonstrating the company’s value relative to peers.
About BTCS
BTCS Inc

is a blockchain technology company focused primarily on infrastructure and services for blockchain networks, with an emphasis on the Ethereum ecosystem. Its activities include operating blockchain validator nodes and participating in staking, which helps support network security and transaction processing while generating rewards for the company.

The company has also pursued decentralized finance and other blockchain-related technologies, including tools and strategies designed to provide exposure to digital assets and blockchain infrastructure.
